notes: Target Home (SR22). Access: direct HTTP fetch (curl_cffi/requests impersonation) of target.com /c/ pages worked cleanly (200s) and exposes the site's own taxonomy tree in embedded __NEXT_DATA__ JSON (children arrays, on-page 'shop by category' taxonomy_nodes modules). Checked for a genuine Bestsellers-type PLP via: (1) the Home department page's own 'New & featured' merchandising module (only exposed New Arrivals, Threshold-new, Fall Decor, Halloween Decor, Humidifiers, Wedding Registry - no bestsellers/popular/trending link); (2) the global top-nav 'Deals' mega menu and its full department list (Sports, Grocery, Beauty, Health, Household, Personal Care, School, Home, Kitchen&Dining, Deals, Clearance - no Bestsellers department); (3) the Home department's full top-level children list (Home Deals, Furniture, Bedding, Kitchen&Dining, Bath, Home Decor, Lighting, Mattresses, Rugs, Storage&Organization, Heating/Cooling, Window Treatments, Vacuums, Appliances, Kids Home, Automotive, Home Improvement, Patio/Lawn/Garden, Teen Room, Wedding Registry - none named Bestsellers/Popular/Top Sellers); (4) site search for 'best sellers' and 'home best sellers' on target.com/s - both resolve only to a generic keyword search-results/SEO landing page (canonical_url /s/best+sellers, type=Search) with no distinct curated listing or stable product count - excluded per brief as a search-results page, not a merchandising PLP; (5) full-text keyword scan of the Home department page HTML for popular, favorite, most-loved, customer favorite, top-selling, top rated, trending - the only 'favorite' hits are the unrelated user wishlist ('favorites list') feature, and the only 'trending' hits are algorithmically personalized 'trending_for_you' product carousels embedded in homepage widgets with no dedicated URL, no stable count, and no site-taxonomy identity as a Bestsellers concept (excluded as personalized recommendation modules, not a browsable PLP). No robots.txt Disallow blocking any of this (checked, no Claude-specific rule). Conclusion: Target does not expose a genuine, site-defined Bestsellers/Best Sellers/Top Sellers/Customer Favorites/Trending Products PLP for its Home department (or site-wide, as far as discoverable via nav+search). This mirrors Target's actual site structure - Target markets 'Deals' and 'Clearance' and 'New Arrivals' as first-class navigable concepts but has no equivalent Bestsellers concept in its /c/ taxonomy.
